summary: Console: Long-running dashboard queries intermittently lose alert context and leave orphaned tracehooks after minutely sampling rollovers
description: Customer reports that several dashboard widgets which run long time-range queries (multi-hour) lose their alert evaluation context intermittently around minute-boundary sampling rollovers. When this happens, alert notifications either fail to include the tracehook link or include a tracehook that no longer resolves (404). The customer sees the alerts still fire in the console but downstream Slack notifications point to broken tracehook URLs, and some tracehook tokens appear in the retention prune logs as being deleted immediately after generation.
impact: Multiple scheduled alerts for FinSight production dashboards are generating Slack notifications with broken tracehook links; customers cannot navigate from the alert to the associated traces. This affects ~6 dashboards and is causing missed triage for strandable production incidents. Estimated affected alert-fires since March 9: ~120. Customer is on Enterprise plan and flagged for elevated support.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Login to FinSight org in console (prod, us-east).
2) Open dashboard 'Realtime Trading Health' with a saved query time-range of last 6h and minutely sampling enabled, set alert to fire on 95th percentile latency over 5m window.
3) Wait for a minute-boundary roll (xx:59 -> yy:00) and observe alert evaluation and notification delivery within the next 2m.
4) Inspect Slack notification payload, copy tracehook URL, and open in browser (or curl) to verify whether trace context resolves.
5) Repeat while toggling sampling frequency between minutely and 30s — issue appears to correlate with minutely sampling buckets and long-running queries.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: retention prune worker runs per-minute job that considers last-seen timestamp and buckets; for very short-lived 'fresh' tokens created during evaluation, the pruning predicate can mis-evaluate bucket boundaries and delete tokens immediately.
Reproduction: reproduced by executing saved query q-773 repeatedly at minute boundary with sampling set to 1m and alert eval window 5m; observed create->prune within 1-3s window.

Root cause theory: retention worker uses sampling_bucket_end timestamp to compute staleness; off-by-one timezone/epoch rounding at minute boundary causes tokens with TTL to be misclassified as expired. Additionally, alerting pipeline emits notification before retention's acknowledgement leading to race.
Related systems: retention-worker-3 (k8s), alert-evaluator v2, notification-queue (async), tracehook-store (redis-index + s3 pointer).
Dashboards & artifacts: linked staging traces at https://console.redwood.ai/trace/q-773/playback?run=replicate-20260310, slack thread #support with logs in /archives/C02.

Countermeasure tested: delaying notification emission by 2s reduced occurrences in staging to 0/1200 evaluated alerts. Permanent fix implemented in PR 4278 to change pruning predicate to use token.creation_timestamp + ttl and atomic mark-before-delete flow.
resolution: Workaround: temporarily change affected alerts to 30s sampling or add 2s eval delay in alerting config to avoid race at minute boundary. Permanent fix: rolled out hotfix 2026-03-12T15:00UTC that updates retention worker to use creation_timestamp + ttl and adds an atomic retention flag for recently-created tracehooks. Canary (10%) showed no regression; full rollout completed 2026-03-12T16:10 UTC. Follow-ups: add unit tests for minute-boundary cases, add e2e test that simulates alerting->retention race, and update runbook 'Tracehook Retention' with troubleshooting steps. Customer validated and confirmed resolution on 2026-03-12.
follow_up_actions: 1) Create unit tests for retention pruning edge cases (assigned to eng:retention team).
2) Add synthetic e2e alert evaluation that runs across minute boundaries in CI (assigned to qa-alerting).
3) Update runbook and add a dashboard to monitor unexpected tracehook deletions (assigned to oncall).
4) Reach out to FinSight CSM to schedule a short recap and close the loop.
